page: OVHcloud r3-32-flex is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on KVM hypervisors. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Each core provides one hardware thread, avoiding simultaneous multithreading overhead. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation stands at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. No discrete GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results reflect robust single-threaded compute and memory subsystem performance alongside moderate multi-core scalability. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core CPU score ranked in the top 25 percent at 3077.37, while multi-core throughput landed in the middle tier at 12265.79. PassMark memory testing placed in the top 25 percent with a score of 2790.5, aligning with high cached read bandwidth of 591.62 GB/sec. Conversely, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 23.99 GB/sec, placing in the lower quartile. Geekbench scores posted 1909.0 for single-core and 5968.0 for multi-core performance, led by strong text processing marks of 2612.0.

From an operational and cost perspective, the instance provides high memory density per compute thread without the premium of oversized vCPU pools. Performance bottlenecks emerge primarily in network-bound scenarios and large uncached memory scans, demonstrated by static web serving throughput measuring 4.83 GB/sec and prompt processing on a 7B model measuring 16.8 tokens/sec. The configuration is best aligned with in-memory caching systems such as Redis, moderate relational databases, backend ETL workers, and memory-dependent data processing tasks.
description: OVHcloud r3-32-flex is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.3 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD on a KVM hypervisor. With an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation and 32 MB of L3 cache, the system targets workloads that require dense memory without demanding excessive CPU concurrency. In synthetic benchmarks, it demonstrates upper-tier single-core CPU execution and PassMark memory performance, balanced by standard multi-core processing and a 1 Gbps network connection. The platform does not incorporate hardware GPU accelerators. The hardware configuration delivers efficient performance for Redis key-value stores, intermediate caching layers, relational database instances, and memory-heavy application runtimes.
